We have applied three templates sequentially, got precursors at each step.

First step (template 324324) gave two products: product1: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1" and product2: "Nc1ccccc1N". That seems to split the amide? Actually original target had ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So after first step we got the amide carbonyl replaced with carboxylic acid? Actually product1 has /C=C/C(=O)O (acid) and product2 is an aniline diamine? Wait product2 is "Nc1ccccc1N" which is p-phenylenediamine? Actually it's an aniline with NH2 at both positions? It's an aniline with two NH? The SMILES "Nc1ccccc1N" is aniline with two NH groups at para? Actually it's aniline with NH at both ends? It's a benzene with two NH substituents at positions 1 and? The SMILES indicates N attached to aromatic carbon at position 1 and N attached to aromatic carbon at position 6? That's p-phenylenediamine.

Second step (template 1914396) applied to product1 gave two products: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" and "O=C(O)CC(=O)O". So the acid side chain turned into aldehyde? Actually product1 now has C=O (aldehyde) attached to aromatic ring, and product2 is succinic acid? O=C(O)CC(=O)O is succinic acid.

Third step (template 733) applied to "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" gave something? We haven't applied yet. Need to apply template 733 to that molecule to get precursors.

Let's apply template 733.
